---
title: Little Pell volunteer weather station, station file
type: source
---

The Little Pell volunteer weather station has been read by hand every morning since 1961.
The equipment is a standard eight inch gauge on a fence post, a graduated cylinder, and a
paper log book carrying the same column headings it was printed with. The current observer,
a retired schoolteacher, took the post over in 1998 and has not missed a morning since.

The county installed an automated tipping bucket sensor 400 feet from the gauge in 2009. The
two instruments stand close enough that a rain event at one is a rain event at the other,
which is why last month's disagreement drew any attention. The volunteer logged 1.3 inches
on the morning of the eighth. The county sensor reported no rain for the same period, and
the state filed that zero as the reading of record.

An inspection in the spring found a wasp nest packed into the funnel of the tipping bucket.
The nest had been in place through two full seasons. Every reading the unit sent to the
state across that stretch carried a QC flag, the automated quality marker the state appends
when a gauge reports values outside the expected band. No one in the county office opened
the flagged records.

The state's regional model gives an independent estimate of monthly rainfall for the grid
square Little Pell sits in. Over the last three years, 91 percent of the volunteer's monthly
totals agree with the regional model to within a tenth of an inch. The sensor's monthly
totals agree with the same model 64 percent of the time over the same stretch.

The town has argued about the gauge across two budget cycles. The position on record is that
a hand reading taken with a graduated cylinder is a hobbyist's number and the wired sensor
is the instrument of record. The inspection report was filed in the spring and has not been
raised at a meeting since.
